Resolves #18800

Five `menu.List` docblocks now describe a submenu rest as started by the pointer or by keyboard focus, which is what the code has done since #18783. Two of them are the public `showSubMenuOnHover` and `subMenuHoverDelay` configs. Comment lines only.

Micro-review eligible: docs — comment-only diff, each sentence checked against the method it describes.

Evidence: L1 (static contract: the diff against `src/menu/List.mjs` at `5d375d9722`) → L1 required (AC-1, AC-2 are about the docs themselves). No residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Witness |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `showSubMenuOnHover`, `subMenuHoverDelay`, `restTimeoutId`, `cancelRest()`, `onItemRest()`. Each claim traces to code: `startRest()` reads both configs for `onFocusMove()` and `onItemMouseEnter()`; each call restarts the one timer, so arrowing past items previews only the one focus stops on; `subMenuHoverDelay: 0` calls `onItemRest()` directly; `selection.menu.ListModel#onKeyDownRight` enters a submenu, showing it first when needed. |
| AC-2 | `git diff -U0` holds no changed line outside a `*` comment line. |

## Test Evidence

No runtime change. The commit hooks' `check-jsdoc-types`, `check-block-alignment`, `check-parse` and `check-whitespace` pass, and no changed line exceeds 120 characters.

## Deltas

- `onItemRest()`'s body said a preview "neither selects nor takes focus". For a focus rest, focus is already on the item, so this now says "moves focus", and `showSubMenuOnHover` uses the same words.
- `showSubMenuOnHover` now names ArrowRight next to click and Enter as a way into the submenu, since a keyboard user meets the preview first.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] None — a docs-only diff has nothing to observe after merge.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** micro — a docs sweep across five docblocks in one file, comment lines only; behaviour-preserving, and the concept it describes was taught by #18783 rather than here.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that these five docblocks still describe a pointer-only rest while the code has had two initiators since #18783, and that every changed sentence traces to the method it describes. Verified at `ba1dca569a`. Comment-only holds mechanically: every added and removed line in the diff begins with `*` inside a docblock, so no code line changed — I checked rather than taking the AC's word, since that is the one claim a docs PR can get wrong invisibly. The substantive claims each land. `startRest()` is called from exactly two places, `onFocusMove()` at `:686` and `onItemMouseEnter()` at `:719`, which is what makes "the pointer **or keyboard focus**" true of both configs rather than of one. `startRest()` opens with `me.cancelRest()`, so "arrowing past items previews only the one focus stops on" is the restart, not a hope. `subMenuHoverDelay: 0` takes the else branch straight into `onItemRest()`, and "0 acts at once" is the right repair of "0 acts on enter", which silently meant *pointer* enter. `ArrowRight` reaching a submenu is `selection.menu.ListModel#onKeyDownRight:53` calling `view.showSubMenu(item.id, record)`, so listing it beside click and Enter is accurate. The one thing I looked for and did not find: a sentence quietly widening beyond the code — "neither selects nor **moves** focus" replacing "takes focus" is if anything the stricter claim, and `showSubMenu(nodeId, record, false)` backs it. This also discharges the nit I raised on #18796, where `cancelRest`'s summary still said *pointer* while `startRest`'s had been updated; filing it separately rather than folding it into a behavioural PR is the right call, since a sweep across five blocks is reviewable on its own terms and would have been invisible inside a four-line fix.
